**Longitudinal Clinical Summary – Tomos Ellis (DOB 17‑May‑2008)**  

**07 Jan 2026 – Emergency Department**  
- Presented with 3‑day history of lower‑abdominal pain, constipation, reduced appetite, mild nausea; pain 7/10, worsened by eating.  
- Examination: mild abdominal distension, lower‑quadrant tenderness, no guarding/rebound, mild dehydration (dry mucous membranes, reduced skin turgor). Vitals stable.  
- Investigations: Full blood count, U&Es, CRP, LFTs – all normal; abdominal X‑ray showed significant faecal loading, no obstruction or perforation.  
- Initial management: NPO, IV 0.9 % NaCl 500 mL over 4 h, single oral dose of bisacodyl 10 mg, oral fluids encouraged.  
- Diagnosis in ED: **Constipation with mild dehydration**.  
- Disposition: Admitted to paediatric ward (Bed C05) under Dr Susan J Robson.  

**07 Jan 2026 – Paediatric Admission (Day 1)**  
- Oral laxative started: Movicol (macrogol) 1 sachet TID (prescribed by Dr Aya Kobayashi).  
- Continued IV fluids for hydration.  
- Nursing and allied‑health education on high‑fibre diet, fluid intake, and mobilisation provided.  

**07 Jan 2026 – Early Ward Review**  
- Dr Yuri Matsumoto (FY1) reiterated plan: macrogol 1 sachet TID, monitor bowel movements, reassess after 24 h; consider further imaging if no improvement.  

**07 Jan 2026 – Ward Round (13:00)**  
- Pain reduced to 5/10 after fluids. Abdomen soft, mildly tender, still distended.  
- Plan modified: macrogol 1 sachet BD, oral fluid intake ≥2 L/day, continue monitoring.  

**07 Jan 2026 – Physiotherapy & Nursing Education**  
- Light mobilisation (walking, seated leg lifts) and education on movement to aid bowel motility.  
- Provided written high‑fibre dietary advice.  

**08 Jan 2026 – Day 2 Review**  
- Partial bowel movement overnight; abdominal pain further reduced, abdomen less distended.  
- Vitals remained stable.  
- Continued macrogol, now documented as 1 sachet TDS.  
- Encouraged oral hydration and aimed for a full bowel movement within 24 h.  

**08 Jan 2026 – Allied‑Health Interventions**  
- Two physiotherapy sessions (10:30 h and 14:00 h) focusing on gentle stretching and continued mobilisation.  
- Dietitian review: high‑fibre diet (whole grains, fresh fruit, vegetables) reinforced; no medication changes.  

**09 Jan 2026 – Day 3 Review & Discharge**  
- Full bowel movement overnight; no abdominal pain, abdomen soft and non‑tender.  
- Macrogol discontinued.  
- Prescribed take‑home lactulose 10 mL BD PRN for constipation maintenance.  
- Discharged with instructions: maintain high‑fibre diet, drink ≥2 L fluids daily, continue light walking at home.  

**Post‑Discharge**  
- Nurse Jamie Leigh Alexander contacted GP (Dr CianCian) to relay discharge summary and arrange follow‑up for constipation prevention.  

**Key Points**  
- **Diagnoses:** Constipation with mild dehydration (resolved).  
- **Investigations:** Abdominal X‑ray (faecal loading), normal blood panel.  
- **Treatments:** IV 0.9 % NaCl, bisacodyl 10 mg PO (single dose), oral macrogol (dose adjusted from TID → BD → TDS), lactulose PRN at discharge, high‑fluid intake, high‑fibre diet, physiotherapy‑guided mobilisation.  
- **Clinical course:** Pain decreased from 7/10 to 0/10; bowel movements progressed from none → partial → full; dehydration corrected; patient discharged home in stable condition.

**Longitudinal Clinical Summary – Allan Victor Robinson, 67 y, NHS 680034032**

**01 Jan 2026 – Emergency Presentation**
- **Event:** Minor fall at home → acute confusion.  
- **Vitals:** BP 170/95 mmHg, HR 88 bpm, RR 16, SpO₂ 98 % (room air).  
- **History:** Hypertension, osteoarthritis; no regular meds, no drug allergies.  
- **Assessments:** GCS 12/15, disoriented to time/place.  
- **Investigations:** Urgent bloods (FBC, electrolytes, coagulation – all normal) and non‑contrast CT head.  
- **CT result:** Subdural hygroma, no mid‑line shift or acute haemorrhage.  
- **Initial Plan:** Admit to Neurology Ward for monitoring; neuro observations q4 h; repeat CT in 48 h; encourage mobilisation as tolerated.

**01 Jan 2026 – In‑patient Management**
- **Physiotherapy (15:30):** Mild gait instability; daily balance/mobility exercises initiated.  
- **Occupational Therapy (17:00):** Mild fine‑motor difficulty (buttoning, utensil handling); OT sessions planned.  
- **Speech & Language Therapy (02 Jan, 14:30):** Swallowing adequate; mild word‑finding difficulty noted, no intervention required.  

**03 Jan 2026 – Physiotherapy Progress**
- Balance/coordination exercises with moderate improvement; stair‑climbing introduced.

**04 Jan 2026 – Ward Review (Dr E. O’Connor)**
- **Repeat CT (03 Jan):** No progression of subdural hygroma.  
- **Clinical status:** More oriented, stable neuro observations, mildly unstable gait.  
- **Plan:** Referral to social work for home assessment; continue daily physio and OT; consider discharge when stable.

**05 Jan 2026 – Clinical Update**
- **Repeat CT (03 Jan):** No progression.  
- **Status:** Patient feels clearer, confident with supervised mobilisation; mild residual gait instability.  
- **New medication:** Atorvastatin 40 mg once daily for 7 days (cardiovascular risk).  
- **Therapy:** Final physiotherapy session confirmed independent mobility; confusion resolved (GCS 15/15).  
- **Social work:** Community support services arranged.

**06 Jan 2026 – Discharge Planning**
- **Status:** Improving confusion, independent mobility, home safety adaptations deemed adequate.  
- **Medications added:** Levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily for 7 days.  
- **Discharge:** Confirmed for 06 Jan; discharge summary and GP letter prepared; neurology outpatient follow‑up scheduled in 1 month; community support and home‑safety advice provided.  
- **Patient education:** Dizziness/confusion management and falls‑prevention advice given.

**07 Jan 2026 – Final Review (Consultant Dr S. Gregory)**
- Patient clinically stable, no residual confusion or neurological deficits.  
- Discharge set for 08 Jan; neuro clinic follow‑up confirmed.

**Overall Course**
- **Primary diagnosis:** Subdural hygroma secondary to minor fall, presenting with acute confusion.  
- **Secondary issues:** Transient mild gait instability, fine‑motor coordination difficulty, mild word‑finding difficulty (all resolved with therapy).  
- **Investigations:** Initial CT head (subdural hygroma); repeat CT on 03 Jan (no progression); routine labs normal.  
- **Treatments:** Neurology admission with regular observations, repeat imaging, physiotherapy (balance, gait, stair climbing), occupational therapy (fine‑motor training), speech‑language assessment, atorvastatin 40 mg OD (7 days), levetiracetam 500 mg BD (7 days).  
- **Outcome:** Confusion resolved, cognition normalized (GCS 15/15), gait stabilized, independent mobility achieved; discharged home with community support and scheduled neurology follow‑up.

**Longitudinal Clinical Summary – Jack Geoffrey Gray (3 y, male)**  

**2026‑01‑06 (Presentation & Admission)**  
- **Chief complaint:** Poor feeding, mild lethargy, reduced urine output.  
- **Initial assessment (A&E):** Temp 38.3 °C, HR 120 bpm, RR 22‑24 /min, SpO₂ 98 % on room air; mild dehydration (dry mucous membranes, capillary refill ≈ 2 s). No respiratory distress, no vomiting/diarrhoea.  
- **Allergies:** Pollen, macrolides. No regular medications, no past medical history.  
- **Diagnoses (ED):** Viral illness (viral upper respiratory tract infection) with mild dehydration.  
- **Interventions (ED):**  
  - Paracetamol suspension 5 mL (120 mg/5 mL) for fever.  
  - Oral fluid bolus 10 mL/kg normal saline (well tolerated).  
  - Plan for oral rehydration solution (ORS) in small, frequent doses.  
- **Admission plan (Paediatric Assessment Unit):** Start IV fluids 0.9 % NaCl + 5 % dextrose at 75 % maintenance, continue ORS, paracetamol PRN, no antibiotics.

**2026‑01‑06 (Early inpatient care)**  
- **Investigations:** Venous blood gas – pH 7.33, HCO₃⁻ 17 mmol/L (mild metabolic acidosis). No other labs performed.  
- **Ongoing treatment:**  
  - IV maintenance fluids (0.9 % NaCl + 5 % dextrose) at 75 % maintenance.  
  - Paracetamol 15 mg/kg q6 h PRN (subsequent doses 5 mL q6 h).  
  - Nasal saline drops (0.9 % saline, 2 drops each nostril PRN).  
  - Encouragement of oral feeds/ORS as tolerated.  
- **Clinical status:** Mildly lethargic but consolable; dry lips, capillary refill ≈ 3 s; nasal congestion present; abdomen soft; no respiratory distress. Vitals: HR 115‑120 bpm, BP 90‑95/50‑60 mmHg, RR 34, Temp 37.9 °C, SpO₂ 98 %.

**2026‑01‑07 (Continued inpatient care)**  
- **Overnight course:** Improved oral intake, no fever, nasal congestion persisted.  
- **Vitals (08:30):** HR 102 bpm, BP 91/58 mmHg, RR 22 /min, Temp 36.9 °C, SpO₂ 98 %.  
- **Management adjustments:**  
  - Reduced IV fluids to 50 % maintenance to promote oral hydration.  
  - Continue PRN paracetamol (120 mg q6 h if needed).  
  - Continue nasal saline drops.  
- **ENT review (11:30):** Moderate nasal mucosal inflammation consistent with viral URTI; no purulent discharge. Added saline nasal spray for irrigation and advised steam inhalation twice daily.  
- **Supportive care:** Ongoing dietary advice (small, frequent feeds, ORS), parental education on dehydration signs and nasal care.

**2026‑01‑08 (Discharge planning & outcome)**  
- **Clinical status (09:00):** Afebrile, alert, playful; mild nasal congestion only; well‑hydrated; oral intake satisfactory. Vitals stable (HR ≈ 100 bpm, BP ≈ 90/60 mmHg, RR 22 /min, Temp 36.8 °C, SpO₂ 98 %).  
- **Discharge orders:**  
  - Paracetamol suspension 120 mg/5 mL PRN for fever or discomfort.  
  - Continue saline nasal drops PRN; initiate saline spray irrigation and steam inhalation twice daily for nasal clearance.  
  - Maintain oral fluids/ORS and small frequent meals at home.  
  - No new medications prescribed.  
- **Education:** Parents instructed on hydration monitoring, signs of deterioration (reduced wet nappies, increased lethargy), nasal care, and when to seek medical help. Contact GP (Dr Liu Tao) advised if symptoms worsen.  

**Summary of Course**  
Jack presented with a viral URTI causing mild dehydration and a transient mild metabolic acidosis. Prompt oral and IV rehydration, antipyretic therapy, and supportive nasal care led to rapid clinical improvement. Fever resolved by the first night, oral intake normalized, and metabolic parameters were not re‑checked but remained clinically stable. He was discharged on 08‑Jan‑2026 in good condition with clear home‑care instructions.

**Longitudinal Clinical Summary – Philip Paul Cook (49‑year‑old male)**  

**02 Jan 2026 – Emergency Department**  
- Presented after a minor fall with acute confusion; GCS 14/15, mild disorientation, no loss of consciousness.  
- Past history: hypertension, mild osteoarthritis. No drug allergies.  
- Neurological assessment showed no focal deficits; pupils slightly delayed bilaterally at 23:15.  
- Urgent CT head performed → subdural hygroma, no mid‑line shift.  
- Laboratory tests: mild hyponatraemia (Na 132 mmol/L); other biochemistry normal.  
- Initial management: IV 0.9 % NaCl 1 L over 8 h, IV paracetamol 1 g QID for pain, dehydration noted, neurological monitoring every 4 h, liaison with neurology.

**03 Jan 2026 – Admission (Neurology)**  
- Subdural hygroma confirmed; neurological status stable, mild fatigue only.  
- Vitals stable; repeat labs pending.  
- Continued IV fluids, oral hydration encouraged, repeat U&E in 24 h.  
- Started prophylactic ceftriaxone 2 g IV daily (day 2 of 5).  
- Initiated daily physiotherapy (gait training with Zimmer frame) and occupational therapy (ADL adaptations, button‑hook tool).  

**04 Jan 2026**  
- Social work assessment for discharge planning and home‑safety needs.  
- OT session focused on ADL adaptations (bed‑to‑chair transfers, adaptive cutlery) and addressed mild fine‑motor difficulty.  

**04 Jan 2026 – Ward Round**  
- Hyponatraemia persisted (Na 133 mmol/L); patient reported mild evening headaches.  
- Management adjusted: fluid restriction to 1.5 L/day, oral sodium chloride 1 g TID, paracetamol 1 g PO PRN for headache.  

**05 Jan 2026**  
- Patient reported improved confidence with mobility; no new symptoms.  
- Hyponatraemia unchanged (Na 133 mmol/L); fluid restriction continued.  
- Sodium chloride reduced to 600 mg TID; physiotherapy continued.  
- OT cognitive rehabilitation introduced (memory, problem‑solving, attention) – mild cognitive difficulties noted.  

**05 Jan 2026 – Family Meeting**  
- Consultant Dr Hassan discussed discharge options with spouse; tentative discharge set for 09 Jan 2026 pending stable neurology and therapy completion.  

**06 Jan 2026**  
- Sodium remained low (Na 132 mmol/L); fluid restriction and oral sodium (1 g TID) maintained.  
- Speech‑language therapy identified mild short‑term memory recall difficulty; cognitive exercises prescribed.  
- OT session reinforced ADL techniques with adaptive tools; occasional verbal prompts required.  

**08 Jan 2026**  
- Neurological status stable, no headache or dizziness; mobility markedly improved, patient ambulating independently.  
- Labs normal; continued paracetamol 500 mg PRN for musculoskeletal discomfort (7‑day course).  
- Discharge planning progressed.  

**09 Jan 2026 – Final Ward Round & Discharge**  
- Subdural hygroma remained stable; mild hyponatraemia (Na 132‑133 mmol/L) addressed with oral sodium supplementation.  
- Patient well, no headache, confusion, or dizziness; ambulating safely with a walking stick.  
- Discharged with:  
  - Paracetamol 500 mg 1‑2 tablets PO QDS PRN for 14 days (and 1 g QDS as per discharge summary).  
  - Fluid intake limited to 1.5 L/day.  
  - Oral sodium chloride tablets (1 g TID).  
  - Fall‑prevention advice and avoidance of anticoagulants unless prescribed.  
  - Adaptive equipment (long‑handled reacher, non‑slip mat, shower chair).  
  - Follow‑up: neurology outpatient clinic in 2 weeks; GP review in 7 days.  
  - Community physiotherapy and occupational therapy arranged.  

**Key Diagnoses**  
- Subdural hygroma (no mid‑line shift)  
- Acute confusion secondary to hygroma and mild hyponatraemia/dehydration  
- Mild hyponatraemia (Na 132‑133 mmol/L)  
- Hypertension (pre‑existing)  
- Mild osteoarthritis (pre‑existing)  

**Overall Course**  
The patient’s acute confusion resolved with correction of dehydration and careful management of hyponatraemia. Neurological status remained stable throughout admission, with progressive improvement in gait and balance via physiotherapy and ADL independence via occupational therapy. Cognitive deficits were mild and addressed with targeted rehabilitation. The patient was safely discharged on 09 Jan 2026 with appropriate medication, fluid‑restriction instructions, adaptive aids, and arranged community follow‑up.

- **Lab:** Na 133 mmol/L.  
- **Plan:** Refer to physiotherapy for advanced mobility/stair‑climbing; continue NaCl 600 mg BD; ongoing neuro monitoring.

- **SLT (11:00):** Speech clear, bedside water swallow test normal, prior word‑finding issue not evident; cleared from speech‑language perspective.  
- **Physiotherapy (16:00):** 20 m unaided walking and small‑step navigation performed safely; gait stable, confidence high; cleared for independent ambulation; continue daily mobility exercises.  

**11‑12 Jan 2026 – Discharge Preparation**
- **Discharge checklist (17:30, 11 Jan):** All items completed; paracetamol 500 mg PRN pain tablets prepared.  
- **Discharge (10 Jan, 12:00):** Patient escorted home, given discharge summary and medication instructions; prescribed paracetamol 1 g Q6 h PRN for headache.  

**Overall Course**
- The patient presented with acute confusion after a minor fall; imaging identified a subdural hygroma without acute bleed.  
- Managed conservatively with neuro observation, blood‑pressure control, analgesia (paracetamol), and electrolyte support.  
- Cognitive deficits were mild and improved with occupational and speech‑language therapy.  
- Functional mobility progressed from assisted to independent ambulation with stair‑climbing ability, supported by physiotherapy and home‑safety modifications.  
- Hyponatraemia was mild and monitored; sodium supplementation (NaCl tablets) continued.  
- The patient was discharged on 12 Jan 2026 with instructions for continued paracetamol PRN and outpatient follow‑up as arranged.

**Longitudinal Clinical Summary – Manveer Kumar (DOB 12/05/1936, NHS 714 471 213)**  

**22 Dec 2025 – Pre‑operative assessment**  
- **Presenting problem:** Severe right‑shoulder pain and stiffness secondary to end‑stage osteoarthritis (OA).  
- **Past medical history:** Hypertension, gastro‑oesophageal reflux disease, cataract surgery (2018).  
- **Medications:** Paracetamol 500 mg PRN, Omeprazole 20 mg daily.  
- **Investigations:** CXR normal, ECG sinus rhythm, full blood count showing mild anaemia (Hb 11.2 g/dL); other labs normal.  
- **Management:** Initiated ferrous sulfate 200 mg twice daily to optimise Hb; cleared for general anaesthesia (GA) by anaesthetic team; written consent obtained for total right‑shoulder replacement.  

**3 Jan 2026 – Admission and Surgery**  
- **Admission:** Elective admission; vitals stable, mild anaemia continued to be managed with ferrous sulfate.  
- **Procedure (09:00 ≈):** Total right‑shoulder replacement via anterior delto‑pectoral approach; cemented modular prosthesis implanted. Intra‑operative findings – severe glenohumeral joint degeneration, no infection; minimal blood loss; no complications.  
- **Anaesthesia:** GA (no intra‑operative issues).  

**Post‑operative course**  

| Date & Time | Clinical events / investigations | Treatment / plan |
|-------------|-----------------------------------|-------------------|
| **03 Jan 2026 18:30** (PACU) | Stable cardiovascular & respiratory status; O₂ 97 % RA; BP 128/76 mmHg; mild nausea. | IV morphine 2 mg for pain, ondansetron 4 mg IV for nausea, IV cefuroxime 1.5 g q8h (24 h), PCA morphine, sling applied, regular paracetamol 1 g q6h, PRN oral morphine 10 mg. |
| **04 Jan 2026 08:30** (ward round) | Mild pain, wound clean, no swelling, vitals stable. | Mobilisation with physiotherapy initiated; enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily for VTE prophylaxis. |
| **04 Jan 2026 10:00** (physio) | Assisted passive ROM, sling education. | Home‑exercise programme demonstrated. |
| **04 Jan 2026 16:00** (ward round) | Mild discomfort, ambulating short distances with assistance; wound still clean. | Added codeine phosphate 30 mg q6h PRN for breakthrough pain; continued enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily. |
| **05 Jan 2026 09:00** (ward round) | Significant improvement in shoulder mobility; pain well‑controlled; wound healing well. | Switched IV paracetamol to oral 500 mg PRN; continued physiotherapy; discharge planned next day. |
| **05 Jan 2026 10:30** (physio) | Active‑assisted ROM, strengthening, self‑care teaching. | No medication changes. |
| **05 Jan 2026 16:00** (ward round) | Minimal pain, further ROM gain; wound clean, no infection. | Prescribed oral paracetamol 500 mg PRN for 7 days; confirmed discharge for the following morning; reinforced home‑exercise instructions. |
| **06 Jan 2026 10:00** (final physio) | Reinforced home‑exercise programme, ADL management; patient engaged and pain‑free. | No new medications. |

**Discharge (planned 06 Jan 2026)**  
- **Medications:** Paracetamol 500 mg PRN (7 days), codeine 30 mg q6h PRN as needed, enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily (to be stopped after hospital stay).  
- **Follow‑up:** Orthopaedic outpatient clinic in 6 weeks.  

**Key diagnoses**  
1. End‑stage osteoarthritis of the right shoulder.  
2. Hypertension (well‑controlled).  
3. Gastro‑oesophageal reflux disease.  
4. Mild pre‑operative anaemia (Hb 11.2 g/dL) – treated with ferrous sulfate.  

**Overall clinical course** – The patient progressed from pre‑operative optimisation (iron supplementation, anaesthetic clearance) to an uncomplicated total right‑shoulder replacement with cemented prosthesis. Post‑operative recovery was uneventful: pain adequately controlled with multimodal analgesia, no infection or vascular complications, early mobilisation and physiotherapy, and successful discharge after five days of inpatient care.

**Longitudinal Clinical Summary – Philip Clive Osborne (Male, DOB 16 Feb 2019)**  

**2024** – Sustained a right‑tibial fracture; treated with internal fixation (metallic device).  

**28 Dec 2025** – Pre‑operative clinic (Dr R. P. Jones, SpR)  
- Planned elective removal of the right‑tibial fixation device on 07 Jan 2026.  
- Past medical history: mild asthma (inhaler‑controlled), eczema, allergies to pollen, nuts, penicillin and sulfonamides.  
- Medications: paracetamol PRN, cetirizine PRN, montelukast 4 mg once daily (started ≈ 2 weeks pre‑op).  
- Examination: well‑appearing, mild bilateral wheeze, right tibial scar clean, full ROM.  
- Investigations ordered: full blood count and coagulation screen (later performed).  

**28 Dec 2025 – 11:00** – Anaesthetic assessment (Dr R. P. Jones)  
- ASA II; GA planned.  
- Pre‑op optimisation: continue montelukast, use salbutamol 2 puffs pre‑induction, avoid penicillin‑ and sulfonamide‑based drugs.  
- Routine FBC and coagulation screen performed (results later deemed satisfactory).  

**28 Dec 2025 – 12:00** – Informed consent (Mrs Emily J. Osborne) obtained by Surgeon Dr C. B. Edwards.  
- Discussed risks (infection, bleeding, anaesthetic complications, delayed healing, fracture).  
- Prophylactic antibiotic plan: IV cefuroxime (alternative ready).  

**28 Dec 2025 – 12:15** – Pre‑op nursing check (Nurse M. Nyoni)  
- Identity, allergies, current meds confirmed.  
- Labs reviewed – satisfactory.  
- Asthma stable; salbutamol 2 puffs prescribed for pre‑op use.  
- Admission scheduled for 07 Jan 2026 15:25, Children’s Orthopaedic Ward (bed C04).  

**07 Jan 2026 – 15:25** – Admission (Dr K. A. Wade, FY1)  
- Vitals stable; surgical site clean; no infection.  
- Pre‑op labs within acceptable limits.  
- Plan: proceed with surgery on 08 Jan 2026, give salbutamol 2 puffs pre‑op, IV cefuroxime prophylaxis, continue paracetamol PRN.  

**07 Jan 2026 – 17:00** – Ward round (Consultant Dr I. Khalid)  
- Patient fit for surgery; confirmed prophylactic cefuroxime 50 mg/kg IV pre‑op.  

**07 Jan 2026 – 18:30** – GP medication reconciliation (Nurse R. Riley): no changes.  

**07 Jan 2026 – 19:15** – Post‑op discharge education (Nurse M. Nyoni)  
- Wound‑care instructions; paracetamol 120 mg/5 mL suspension prescribed PRN.  

**08 Jan 2026 – 09:30** – Surgery (Surgeon Dr C. B. Edwards, GA by Dr R. P. Jones)  
- Removal of right‑tibial internal fixation device; device intact, surrounding tissue healthy.  
- Minimal blood loss (<10 mL); no intra‑operative complications.  
- Prophylaxis: cefuroxime suspension 50 mg/kg × 5 days (alternative flagged).  
- Analgesia: paracetamol PRN; discharge plan for next day.  

**08 Jan 2026 – 11:00** – PACU recovery (Dr R. P. Jones)  
- Stable respiratory and cardiovascular status; SpO₂ ≥ 98 % on room air.  
- Pain managed with oral ibuprofen 100 mg; dressing intact.  
- Additional prophylactic antibiotic prescribed: co‑amoxiclav suspension 125/31 mg/5 mL × 5 days (recorded in recovery note).  

**08 Jan 2026 – 14:00** – Ward round (Dr R. P. Jones) – POD 1  
- Surgical site clean, dressing intact; CRP 12 mg/L (post‑op inflammation).  
- Plan: 48‑hour IV cefuroxime course, continue paracetamol PRN, monitor CRP.  

**08 Jan 2026 – 15:30** – Physiotherapy (S. G. Francis)  
- Weight‑bearing tolerated; gentle ankle/knee ROM exercises initiated.  
- Assisted ambulation with child‑size frame; plan supervised mobility twice daily.  

**08 Jan 2026 – 17:00** – Occupational therapy (J. A. Ryan)  
- Safe mobilisation techniques taught; pediatric crutch fitted; home practice advised.  

**08 Jan 2026 – 18:30** – GP update (Nurse M. Nyoni) – contact with Dr Y. E. Walker.  

**09 Jan 2026 – 08:30** – Ward round (Dr R. P. Jones) – POD 2  
- Surgical site clean, no infection; pain well‑controlled with paracetamol.  
- Plan: discharge later that day; prescribe ibuprofen 100 mg suspension TDS for additional analgesia; provide discharge summary.  

**09 Jan 2026 – 10:00** – Physiotherapy (S. G. Francis)  
- Independent ambulation on ward, no limp or discomfort; home exercise programme advised; no further in‑hospital physio required.  

**09 Jan 2026 – 12:00** – GP notified of discharge (Nurse J. Webb).
